reason: Two composer send defects. (1) SessionsPage submit left Subagents (and SSH targets, project model context, a subagent's parent messages) out of its tool-result consent decision, so a Subagents provider conversation on a cloud provider with no command runtime never asked and Core refused every send. The composer now mirrors Core's tool families (chatToolResultConsent.ts), and Core's refusal carries code tool_result_consent_required plus an operator_detail naming the families, so the composer also asks, and resends once with consent, for tools only Core sees (project web search, skill resources). A declined share or a text-only runtime now explains in place and keeps the message; a Core-requested decline returns the message to the composer. (2) prepareProviderCredential threw Error(undefined) for an unknown or unreadable credential state and the send was dropped behind the generic fallback; every state, an unreadable answer and an unreachable Core now name what failed and the next action, and the message is kept. Python covers the typed refusal in ChatService and the 409 API envelope, plus the chat, subagent, harness provider-subagent and preflight files whose tool-enablement path changed. Frontend covers the consent helpers, the credential states, full-App send journeys (consent asked/declined/Core-requested/credential) and the existing App and Subagents-choice journeys through SessionsPage. Playwright runs entry:assistant on desktop, mobile Chromium and mobile WebKit (SessionsPage changed; two new mocked journeys) and area:chat-subagents.
exclusions: Full suites are not approved and are excluded. Harness consent (MCP servers, browser control, agent messaging) is unchanged in behaviour and harness adapters are not selected beyond test_harness_provider_subagents.py. Credential storage (credentials.py) is unchanged, so tests/v3/test_credentials.py is not selected. Mission, native Rust/Tauri and real-Core Playwright areas are not selected: the consent journey was exercised against a scratch real Core (OpenRouter deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash, LAN origin, production bundle) and recorded in the PR body; committed real-Core coverage would need a cloud-classified provider stub.
